issues.failure_explanation: Property (P1) claims that the diagonal elements of the reduction matrix satisfy $|a_{n,n}| \ge \gamma \sigma_{n+b-1}$. The proof asserts that for $n \in (\undertilde{n}, \widetilde{n}]$, $|a_{n,n}| = \sigma_n(f_n) \ge \sigma_{\widetilde{n}}(f_n) \ge \sigma_{\widetilde{n}+1}(f_{\widetilde{n}+1})$. This inference is mathematically false: for any $n < \widetilde{n}$, $f_n$ is one of the spanning elements of $V_{\widetilde{n}}$, which implies $\sigma_{\widetilde{n}}(f_n) = \dist(f_n, V_{\widetilde{n}}) = 0$, whereas $\sigma_{\widetilde{n}+1}(f_{\widetilde{n}+1}) > 0$ in general. More fundamentally, because all $b$ snapshots of a batch are chosen simultaneously using the error surrogate from the beginning of the batch without updating the subspace, intermediate snapshots can be arbitrarily close to earlier snapshots in the same batch. Hence $\dist(f_n, V_n) = |a_{n,n}|$ can be arbitrarily small (or zero), violating $|a_{n,n}| \ge \gamma \sigma_{n+b-1}$. The exact same failure occurs in Lemma A.1 (La:Psbg_B) in the Banach space setting.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must establish a valid lower bound on the batch reduction matrix diagonal entries (or develop a completely new proof architecture that does not rely on term-by-term lower bounds on $a_{n,n}$), which would require restricting the batch selection mechanism to prevent near-collinearity of snapshots within a batch.
issues.overall_effect: All theoretical convergence results for the parallel batch greedy algorithm collapse. Specifically, Theorem 3.3, Theorem 3.4 (polynomial and exponential decay rates), Corollary 3.6, Theorem A.2, and Theorem A.3 are left unproved and unreliable.
issues.title: False lower bound on diagonal elements of the batch greedy reduction matrix
issues.why_classification: Property (P1) is the foundation of the entire convergence analysis in both Hilbert and Banach spaces. Its failure invalidates all convergence theorems and rates claimed in the paper, and resolving it requires new proof architecture or substantial modifications to the algorithm guarantees.
